newsitem.title: UK: Copper snaps higher by close as spreads widen.
newsitem.headline: Copper snaps higher by close as spreads widen.

text.p: London Metal Exchange copper prices held in the spotlight upto Wednesday's close as benchmark three months delivery snapped higher against the background of speculative short-covering on nearby spreads.
Other metals failed to match the gains in copper, with some drifting below Tuesday's closing levels.
Speculative borrowing of the spreads continued to dominate as the sensitive December 16/18 dates approached. This could could impact on the forward market, traders said.
Copper's cash to three months backwardation was last indicated at $270/$280, after an earlier move to $230.
Last three months business was at $2,272, against Tuesday's $2,258 close.
Traders said they expected a period of volatility ahead of the December dates and did not rule out a test of recent eight month highs of $2,285.
They also noted the New York market will be closed on Thursday and Friday for Thanksgiving.
Though the recent tightness has lent robust support to the market traders will continue to eye the LME stock figures.
Several suggest inventories will rise over the coming weeks.
Aluminium after earlier peaking at $1,556 drifted back under profit-taking.
Several traders still believed aluminium could move higher over the coming weeks, against the backdrop of uptrending charts, consumer demand and recent declines in LME inventories.
Nickel dipped back to $7,020, down $45. Traders said light trade liquidation was noted in nickel after recent stock rises.
Lead moved lower after sell-stops were triggered below $700. and it last traded at $694, a loss of $20.
Zinc finished lower at $1,076, versus $1,084, tin settled at $6,095, a loss of $65, and alloy was last quoted at $1,385/90, up $10.
